p: burden of Babylon: That is, the great calamity which was prophesied to come on Babel, a grievous burden which they were not able to bear. In these twelve chapters following he speaks of the plagues with which God would smite the strange nations (whom they knew) to declare that God chastised the Israelites as his children and these others as his enemies: and also that if God does not spare these who are ignorant, they must not think strange if he punishes them who have knowledge of his Law, and do not keep it.
hand: That is, the Medes and Persians.
sanctified ones: That is, prepared and appointed to execute my judgments.
highness: Who willingly go about to the work to which I appoint them, but how the wicked do this, read Isa 10:6.
weapons of his indignation: The army of the Medes and the Persians against Babylon.
flames: The Babylonians anger and grief will be so much that their faces will burn as fire.
stars of heaven and its constellations: They who are overcome will think that all the powers of heaven and earth are against them, Eze 32:7, Joe 3:15, Mt 24:29.
world for their evil: He compares Babylon to the whole world because they so esteemed themselves by reason of their great empire.
proud to cease: He notes the principal vice, to which they are most given as are all that abound in wealth.
man more rare than fine gold: He notes the great slaughter that will be, seeing the enemy will neither for gold or silver spare a man's life as in Isa 13:17.
it shall be as the chased: Meaning the power of Babylon with their hired soldiers.
children also shall be dashed to: This was not accomplished when Cyrus took Babylon, but after the death of Alexander the great.
Arabian pitch tent there: Who used to go from country to country to find pasture for their beasts, but they will find none.
wild beasts of the desert shall: Who were either wild beasts or fools, or wicked spirits, by which Satan deluded man, as by the fairies, goblins, and such like fantasies.
